# PROBLEM STATEMENT :

&nbsp;

At modern road intersections, automated traffic signal lights are the primary safety mechanism regulating vehicular movement and pedestrian crossings. When a critical signal lamp abruptly fails due to a blown fuse, filament burnout, or severed power delivery, intersection navigation becomes ambiguous, exponentially increasing the risk of severe vehicular collisions and traffic deadlocks. Conventional signal systems lack autonomous optical feedback; municipal authorities often remain unaware of a physical dark failure until motorists report an accident or manual inspections occur. Consequently, there is a critical need for an autonomous, low-latency, and cost-effective optical fault detection system that actively verifies the illumination state of each signal fixture and triggers an instantaneous fail-safe alert the moment a light output is lost.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

## AIM :

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;To design and construct an LDR-based traffic alert system that keeps the buzzer OFF under sufficient light and automatically triggers a BUZZER ALARM when light is absent, alerting respective officers.

#### WORKING :

&nbsp;

Light Available / Normal State (Light Present):

&nbsp;

When light falls on the LDR sensor, its resistance remains LOW.&nbsp;&nbsp;

The control circuit keeps the buzzer output OFF (Silent).&nbsp;&nbsp;

Traffic signals function normally without triggering any alert.&nbsp;&nbsp;

&nbsp;

No Light (Light Absent ):

.

When Traffic light is Fails (  due to a blown fuse, filament burnout, or severed power delivery ), the LDR resistance increases significantly.&nbsp;&nbsp;

The control circuit senses this change and automatically turns ON the Buzzer Alarm.&nbsp;&nbsp;

The loud buzzer alert and notifies the respective officers, indicating the traffic light is not working properly.
